question: You are migrating workloads to the cloud. The goal of the migration is to serve customers worldwide as quickly as possible According to local regulations, certain data is required to be stored in a specific geographic area, and it can be served worldwide. You need to design the architecture and deployment for your workloads. What should you do?

options.A: Select a public cloud provider that is only active in the required geographic area
options.B: Select a private cloud provider that globally replicates data storage for fast data access
options.C: Select a public cloud provider that guarantees data location in the required geographic area
options.D: Select a private cloud provider that is only active in the required geographic area

explanations.A: Incorrect. A provider active only in one geographic area cannot serve customers worldwide quickly, which is the primary goal of the migration.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Globally replicating the data would violate the data-residency regulation that requires certain data to remain in a specific geographic area.
explanations.C: Correct. A public cloud provider with a global footprint that also lets you pin data to a specific region (data residency) satisfies both the regulatory storage requirement and the goal of serving customers worldwide quickly.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A private cloud limited to one geographic area lacks the global reach needed to serve customers worldwide with low latency.

question: Your organization needs a large amount of extra computing power within the next two weeks. After those two weeks, the need for the additional resources will end. Which is the most cost-effective approach?

options.A: Use a committed use discount to reserve a very powerful virtual machine
options.B: Purchase one very powerful physical computer
options.C: Start a very powerful virtual machine without using a committed use discount
options.D: Purchase multiple physical computers and scale workload across them

explanations.A: Incorrect. Committed use discounts (CUDs) require a 1-year or 3-year commitment, so they are not cost-effective for a need that lasts only two weeks.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Buying physical hardware is a large capital expense that is wasteful for a short-term, two-week need.
explanations.C: Correct. On-demand (pay-as-you-go) virtual machines let you spin up exactly the capacity you need and shut it down after two weeks, paying only for what you use with no long-term commitment.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Purchasing multiple physical computers is even more expensive and slow to provision, and the hardware would sit idle after two weeks.

question: Your organization needs to plan its cloud infrastructure expenditures. Which should your organization do?

options.A: Review cloud resource costs frequently, because costs change often based on use
options.B: Review cloud resource costs annually as part of planning your organization's overall budget
options.C: If your organization uses only cloud resources, infrastructure costs are no longer part of your overall budget
options.D: Involve fewer people in cloud resource planning than your organization did for on-premises resource planning

explanations.A: Correct. Cloud spending follows a consumption-based (pay-as-you-go) model, so costs vary with usage and should be reviewed frequently to detect changes and optimize spend.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Reviewing only once a year is too infrequent for variable, usage-based cloud costs and can lead to budget surprises.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Cloud infrastructure still incurs operational costs that remain a real part of the overall budget; spending does not disappear because it is in the cloud.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Cloud cost management benefits from broad collaboration across teams; reducing the people involved weakens governance and accountability.

question: The operating systems of some of your organization's virtual machines may have a security vulnerability. How can your organization most effectively identify all virtual machines that do not have the latest security update?

options.A: View the Security Command Center to identify virtual machines running vulnerable disk images
options.B: View the Compliance Reports Manager to identify and download a recent PCI audit
options.C: View the Security Command Center to identify virtual machines started more than 2 weeks ago
options.D: View the Compliance Reports Manager to identify and download a recent SOC 1 audit

explanations.A: Correct. Security Command Center scans your environment and surfaces vulnerabilities, including VMs running disk images with known security issues, which is exactly what is needed here.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The Compliance Reports Manager provides Google's third-party audit reports (like PCI DSS); it does not scan your individual VMs for missing OS updates.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The age of a VM since it was started does not reliably indicate whether its OS is missing the latest security update.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A SOC 1 audit report concerns financial-reporting controls and does not identify vulnerable VMs in your environment.

question: You are currently managing workloads running on Windows Server for which your company owns the licenses. Your workloads are only needed during working hours, which allows you to shut down the instances during the weekend. Your Windows Server licenses are up for renewal in a month, and you want to optimize your license cost. What should you do?

options.A: Renew your licenses for an additional period of 3 years. Renew your licenses for an additional period of 3 years. Negotiate a
options.B: Renew your licenses for an additional period of 2 years. Negotiate a cost reduction by committing to an automatic renewal
options.C: Migrate the workloads to Compute Engine with a bring-your-own-license (BYOL) model
options.D: Migrate the workloads to Compute Engine with a pay-as-you-go (PAYG) model

explanations.A: Incorrect. Committing to a new multi-year license renewal locks in cost even though the workloads run only during working hours, missing the chance to optimize.
explanations.B: Incorrect. A 2-year auto-renewal still pays for licensing during weekends and idle periods, which does not optimize cost for intermittently used workloads.
explanations.C: Incorrect. BYOL typically requires licensing for the full term regardless of usage, so it does not capture savings from shutting instances down on weekends.
explanations.D: Correct. Compute Engine pay-as-you-go (PAYG) Windows licensing is billed per-second only while instances run, so shutting them down on weekends directly reduces license costs.

question: Your organization runs a distributed application in the Compute Engine virtual machines. Your organization needs redundancy, but it also needs extremely fast communication (less than 10 milliseconds) between the parts of the application in different virtual machines. Where should your organization locate this virtual machines?

options.A: In a single zone within a single region
options.B: In different zones within a single region
options.C: In multiple regions, using one zone per region
options.D: In multiple regions, using multiple zones per region

explanations.A: Incorrect. A single zone offers the lowest latency but provides no redundancy, since a zone failure would take down the entire application.
explanations.B: Correct. Placing VMs in different zones of the same region gives redundancy against a single-zone failure while keeping inter-zone latency very low (typically under 10 ms).
explanations.C: Incorrect. Spreading VMs across multiple regions introduces cross-region network latency that usually exceeds the 10 ms requirement.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Multiple regions with multiple zones maximizes redundancy but adds significant cross-region latency, violating the under-10 ms communication requirement.

question: An organization decides to migrate their on-premises environment to the cloud. They need to determine which resource components still need to be assigned ownership. Which two functions does a public cloud provider own? (Choose two.)

explanations.A: Correct. Under the shared responsibility model, the cloud provider owns and maintains the physical hardware, so hardware maintenance is the provider's responsibility.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The customer designs how their own infrastructure is architected on top of the provider's platform; this remains the customer's responsibility.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Automating deployment of the customer's infrastructure and applications is configured and owned by the customer.
explanations.D: Correct. The provider manages the physical capacity of the data centers, ensuring hardware resources are available to scale, so hardware capacity management is the provider's responsibility.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Application security and fixing flaws in the customer's own code is the customer's responsibility under the shared responsibility model.

question: You are a program manager within a Software as a Service (SaaS) company that offers rendering software for animation studios. Your team needs the ability to allow scenes to be scheduled at will and to be interrupted at any time to restart later. Any individual scene rendering takes less than 12 hours to complete, and there is no service-level agreement (SLA) for the completion time for all scenes. Results will be stored in a global Cloud Storage bucket. The compute resources are not bound to any single geographical location. This software needs to run on Google Cloud in a cost-optimized way. What should you do?

options.A: Deploy the application on Compute Engine using preemptible instances
options.B: Develop the application so it can run in an unmanaged instance group
options.C: Create a reservation for the minimum number of Compute Engine instances you will use
options.D: Start more instances with fewer virtual centralized processing units (vCPUs) instead of fewer instances with more vCPUs

explanations.A: Correct. Preemptible (Spot) VMs are heavily discounted and can be interrupted at any time; since the workload is fault-tolerant, has no SLA, and each task finishes within hours, they are the most cost-optimized choice.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Using an unmanaged instance group does not by itself lower compute cost; the cost savings here come from the pricing model, not the grouping method.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Reservations guarantee capacity at standard on-demand pricing and provide no discount, so they are not the most cost-optimized option for interruptible work.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Changing the ratio of instances to vCPUs does not reduce the fundamental compute price; it does not address cost optimization for this interruptible workload.

question: Your manager wants to restrict communication of all virtual machines with internet access; with resources in another network; or with a resource outside Compute Engine. It is expected that different teams will create new folders and projects in the near future. How would you restrict all virtual machines from having an external IP address?

options.A: Define an organization policy at the root organization node to restrict virtual machine instances from having an external IP
options.B: Define an organization policy on all existing folders to define a constraint to restrict virtual machine instances from having
options.C: Define an organization policy on all existing projects to restrict virtual machine instances from having an external IP address
options.D: Communicate with the different teams and agree that each time a virtual machine is created, it must be configured without

explanations.A: Correct. An organization policy applied at the root organization node is inherited by all current and future folders and projects, so the constraint automatically covers new resources teams will create.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Applying the policy only to existing folders would not cover new folders created later, leaving gaps in enforcement.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Applying the policy only to existing projects would not cover the new projects teams are expected to create in the future.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Relying on manual agreement is error-prone and not enforceable; a technical organization policy is required to reliably restrict external IPs.

question: Your multinational organization has servers running mission-critical workloads on its premises around the world. You want to be able to manage these workloads consistently and centrally, and you want to stop managing infrastructure. What should your organization do?

options.A: Migrate the workloads to a public cloud
options.B: Migrate the workloads to a central office building
options.C: Migrate the workloads to multiple local co-location facilities
options.D: Migrate the workloads to multiple local private clouds

explanations.A: Correct. A public cloud lets a multinational organization manage workloads consistently and centrally through one platform while the provider handles the underlying infrastructure, so you stop managing hardware.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Consolidating into one office building still requires you to own and manage all the physical infrastructure yourself.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Co-location facilities still leave you responsible for managing your own servers and infrastructure, just in someone else's building.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Multiple local private clouds add management overhead and do not relieve you of running the infrastructure.

question: Your organization stores highly sensitive data on-premises that cannot be sent over the public internet. The data must be processed both on-premises and in the cloud. What should your organization do?

options.A: Configure Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) in your Google Cloud VPC network
options.B: Create a Cloud VPN tunnel between Google Cloud and your data center
options.C: Order a Partner Interconnect connection with your network provider
options.D: Enable Private Google Access in your Google Cloud VPC network

explanations.A: Incorrect. Identity-Aware Proxy controls user access to applications based on identity; it does not provide a private network path that avoids the public internet.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Cloud VPN encrypts traffic but still routes it over the public internet, which violates the requirement that the data not traverse the public internet.
explanations.C: Correct. Partner Interconnect provides a private, dedicated connection between your on-premises network and Google Cloud through a service provider, so sensitive data never traverses the public internet.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Private Google Access lets VMs without external IPs reach Google APIs; it does not create private connectivity between on-premises and the cloud.

question: Your company's development team is building an application that will be deployed on Cloud Run. You are designing a CI/CD pipeline so that any new version of the application can be deployed in the fewest number of steps possible using the CI/CD pipeline you are designing. You need to select a storage location for the images of the application after the CI part of your pipeline has built them. What should you do?

options.A: Create a Compute Engine image containing the application
options.B: Store the images in Container Registry
options.C: Store the images in Cloud Storage
options.D: Create a Compute Engine disk containing the application

explanations.A: Incorrect. A Compute Engine machine image is for VMs, not for the container images that Cloud Run deploys.
explanations.B: Correct. Container Registry (or Artifact Registry) is the native store for container images, and Cloud Run deploys directly from it, minimizing deployment steps.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Cloud Storage stores objects/files, not container images in a form Cloud Run can deploy directly, so it adds extra steps.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A Compute Engine disk holds VM data, not container images, and Cloud Run cannot deploy an application from it.

question: Each of the three cloud service models - infrastructure as a service (IaaS), platform as a service (PaaS), and software as a service (SaaS) - offers benefits between flexibility and levels of management by the cloud provider and the customer. Why would SaaS be the right choice of service model?

options.A: You want a balance between flexibility for the customer and the level of management by the cloud provider
options.B: You want to minimize the level of management by the customer
options.C: You want to maximize flexibility for the customer.
options.D: You want to be able to shift your emphasis between flexibility and management by the cloud provider as business needs

explanations.A: Incorrect. A balance between flexibility and provider management describes PaaS, not SaaS.
explanations.B: Correct. SaaS delivers a fully managed application, so the provider handles everything and the customer's management burden is minimized.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Maximizing customer flexibility points to IaaS, where the customer controls the OS and runtime, not SaaS.
explanations.D: Incorrect. SaaS is a fixed, fully managed offering; it does not let you dynamically shift the balance between flexibility and management.

question: As your organization increases its release velocity, the VM-based application upgrades take a long time to perform rolling updates due to OS boot times. You need to make the application deployments faster. What should your organization do?

options.A: Migrate your VMs to the cloud, and add more resources to them
options.C: Increase the resources of your VMs

explanations.A: Incorrect. Moving VMs to the cloud and adding resources does not eliminate the OS boot time that is slowing rolling updates.
explanations.B: Correct. Containers share the host OS and start almost instantly, removing the lengthy OS boot times of VMs and making rolling deployments much faster.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Adding CPU or memory does not significantly reduce OS boot time, which is the root cause of slow updates.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Automating rollouts helps consistency but the individual updates would still be slow because each VM must boot its OS.

question: Your organization uses Active Directory to authenticate users. Users' Google account access must be removed when their Active Directory account is terminated. How should your organization meet this requirement?

options.A: Configure two-factor authentication in the Google domain
options.B: Remove the Google account from all IAM policies
options.C: Configure BeyondCorp and Identity-Aware Proxy in the Google domain
options.D: Configure single sign-on in the Google domain

explanations.A: Incorrect. Two-factor authentication strengthens login security but does not tie Google access to the lifecycle of the Active Directory account.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Manually removing accounts from IAM policies is error-prone and does not automatically happen when the AD account is terminated.
explanations.C: Incorrect. BeyondCorp and Identity-Aware Proxy enforce context-aware access to applications but do not federate identity to automatically revoke access on AD termination.
explanations.D: Correct. Configuring single sign-on (SSO) federates authentication to Active Directory, so when the AD account is terminated the user can no longer sign in to Google services.

question: Your company has recently acquired three growing startups in three different countries. You want to reduce overhead in infrastructure management and keep your costs low without sacrificing security and quality of service to your customers. How should you meet these requirements?

options.A: Host all your subsidiaries' services on-premises together with your existing services.
options.B: Host all your subsidiaries' services together with your existing services on the public cloud.
options.C: Build a homogenous infrastructure at each subsidiary, and invest in training their engineers.
options.D: Build a homogenous infrastructure at each subsidiary, and invest in hiring more engineers.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Hosting everything on-premises increases capital cost and management overhead and does not scale easily across multiple countries.
explanations.B: Correct. Consolidating all services on a public cloud reduces infrastructure management overhead, lowers cost through pay-as-you-go pricing, and provides the provider's built-in security and global quality of service.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Building and staffing separate infrastructure at each subsidiary increases management overhead and cost rather than reducing it.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Hiring more engineers to run duplicated infrastructure at each site raises cost and overhead, the opposite of the goal.

question: What is the difference between Standard and Coldline storage?

options.A: Coldline storage is for data for which a slow transfer rate is acceptable.
options.B: Standard and Coldline storage have different durability guarantees.
options.C: Standard and Coldline storage use different APIs.
options.D: Coldline storage is for infrequently accessed data.

explanations.A: Incorrect. All Cloud Storage classes offer the same low-latency, high-throughput access; the difference is access frequency and cost, not transfer speed.
explanations.B: Incorrect. All Cloud Storage classes provide the same 11 nines durability; durability does not differ between classes.
explanations.C: Incorrect. All storage classes use the same Cloud Storage API; only pricing and intended access patterns differ.
explanations.D: Correct. Coldline is designed for infrequently accessed data with lower storage cost but higher retrieval cost, whereas Standard is for frequently accessed (hot) data.

question: What would provide near-unlimited availability of computing resources without requiring your organization to procure and provision new equipment?

explanations.A: Correct. A public cloud provides on-demand, near-unlimited capacity from the provider's data centers, so you scale without buying or provisioning your own hardware.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Containers are a packaging and runtime technology; they still need underlying compute capacity that must be provided somewhere.
explanations.C: Incorrect. A private cloud runs on your own finite hardware, which you must still procure and provision.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Microservices are an application architecture pattern and do not provide computing capacity on their own.

question: You are a program manager for a team of developers who are building an event-driven application to allow users to follow one another's activities in the app. Each time a user adds himself as a follower of another user, a write occurs in the real-time database. The developers will develop a lightweight piece of code that can respond to database writes and generate a notification to let the appropriate users know that they have gained new followers. The code should integrate with other cloud services such as Pub/Sub, Firebase, and Cloud APIs to streamline the orchestration process. The application requires a platform that automatically manages underlying infrastructure and scales to zero when there is no activity. Which primary compute resource should your developers select, given these requirements?

explanations.A: Incorrect. GKE requires you to manage clusters and nodes and does not natively scale to zero, making it heavier than needed for lightweight event handlers.
explanations.B: Correct. Cloud Functions is a serverless, event-driven platform that runs lightweight code in response to triggers (like database writes), integrates with Pub/Sub and Firebase, and scales to zero when idle.
explanations.C: Incorrect. App Engine flexible environment runs on VMs that keep at least one instance running, so it does not scale to zero.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Compute Engine provides VMs that you must manage and that do not automatically scale to zero, which contradicts the serverless requirement.

question: Your organization is developing an application that will capture a large amount of data from millions of different sensor devices spread all around the world. Your organization needs a database that is suitable for worldwide, high-speed data storage of a large amount of unstructured data. Which Google Cloud product should your organization choose?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Firestore is a document database good for app data and offline sync, but it is not optimized for the extremely high-throughput time-series/IoT ingestion described here.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Cloud Data Fusion is a data integration (ETL) service, not a database for storing high-volume sensor data.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Cloud SQL is a relational database for structured data and does not scale to the massive, high-speed unstructured IoT workloads described.
explanations.D: Correct. Cloud Bigtable is a wide-column NoSQL database built for very high write throughput and low latency at massive scale, making it ideal for IoT/sensor and time-series data.

question: Your organization needs to build streaming data pipelines. You don't want to manage the individual servers that do the data processing in the pipelines. Instead, you want a managed service that will automatically scale with the amount of data to be processed. Which Google Cloud product or feature should your organization choose?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Pub/Sub is a messaging service for ingesting and delivering events; it transports data but does not process the data in a pipeline.
explanations.B: Correct. Dataflow is a fully managed, serverless service for stream (and batch) data processing that autoscales with the volume of data, removing the need to manage servers.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Data Catalog is a metadata management and data discovery service, not a data-processing pipeline engine.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Dataprep is for visually exploring and preparing/cleaning data, not for building autoscaling streaming processing pipelines.

question: Your organization is building an application running in Google Cloud. Currently, software builds, tests, and regular deployments are done manually, but you want to reduce work for the team. Your organization wants to use Google Cloud managed solutions to automate your build, testing, and deployment process. Which Google Cloud product or feature should your organization use?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Cloud Scheduler is a managed cron service for triggering scheduled jobs, not a CI/CD build-and-deploy system.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Cloud Code provides IDE plugins to help developers write and debug applications, not to automate the build/test/deploy pipeline.
explanations.C: Correct. Cloud Build is Google Cloud's managed CI/CD service that automatically builds, tests, and deploys applications, reducing manual work.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Deployment Manager provisions infrastructure via templates (infrastructure as code); it does not run the build-and-test CI/CD pipeline.

question: Which Google Cloud product can report on and maintain compliance on your entire Google Cloud organization to cover multiple projects?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Cloud Logging collects and stores logs but does not by itself report on or maintain organization-wide compliance posture.
explanations.B: Incorrect. IAM controls who can do what on resources; it manages access, not compliance reporting across the organization.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Google Cloud Armor protects applications from web attacks and DDoS; it is not a compliance-reporting tool.
explanations.D: Correct. Security Command Center provides centralized visibility, vulnerability and compliance reporting across your entire organization spanning multiple projects.

question: Your organization needs to establish private network connectivity between its on-premises network and its workloads running in Google Cloud. You need to be able to set up the connection as soon as possible. Which Google Cloud product or feature should you use?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Cloud Interconnect provides dedicated physical connectivity but requires provisioning physical circuits, which takes weeks, so it cannot be set up as soon as possible.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Direct Peering connects to Google's network for public services and also requires physical provisioning; it is not a quick private VPC connection.
explanations.C: Correct. Cloud VPN creates an encrypted IPsec tunnel over the internet to your VPC and can be configured quickly, satisfying the need to connect as soon as possible.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Cloud CDN caches and delivers content to end users; it does not provide private connectivity between on-premises and Google Cloud.

question: Your organization is developing a mobile app and wants to select a fully featured cloud-based compute platform for it. Which Google Cloud product or feature should your organization use?

explanations.A: Incorrect. GKE is a container orchestration platform; it is not a purpose-built, fully featured mobile app development platform.
explanations.B: Correct. Firebase is Google's fully featured mobile and web app development platform, providing backend services such as databases, authentication, messaging, and hosting tailored to mobile apps.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Cloud Functions runs individual event-driven functions; it is not a complete mobile app platform on its own.
explanations.D: Incorrect. App Engine hosts web application backends but is not a dedicated mobile development platform with mobile-specific services like Firebase.

question: Your company has been using a shared facility for data storage and will be migrating to Google Cloud. One of the internal applications uses Linux custom images that need to be migrated. Which Google Cloud product should you use to maintain the custom images?

explanations.A: Incorrect. App Engine flexible environment runs your code in Google-managed containers; it does not let you import and maintain your own custom VM disk images.
explanations.B: Correct. Compute Engine lets you import, store, and maintain custom Linux VM images and launch instances from them, which is exactly what the migrated application needs.
explanations.C: Incorrect. App Engine standard environment is a sandboxed runtime that does not support custom VM images.
explanations.D: Incorrect. GKE runs container images, not custom VM machine images, so it is not the right fit for maintaining Linux custom images.

question: Your organization wants to migrate its data management solutions to Google Cloud because it needs to dynamically scale up or down and to run transactional SQL queries against historical data at scale. Which Google Cloud product or service should your organization use?

explanations.A: Incorrect. BigQuery is an analytics data warehouse optimized for OLAP queries, not for high-volume transactional (OLTP) SQL workloads.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Cloud Bigtable is a NoSQL wide-column store and does not support transactional relational SQL queries.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Pub/Sub is a messaging service, not a transactional SQL database.
explanations.D: Correct. Cloud Spanner is a horizontally scalable, strongly consistent relational database that supports transactional SQL and scales up or down to virtually unlimited size.

question: Your organization needs to categorize objects in a large group of static images using machine learning. Which Google Cloud product or service should your organization use?

explanations.A: Incorrect. BigQuery ML builds models from structured data using SQL; it is not designed to classify objects within images.
explanations.B: Incorrect. AutoML Video Intelligence analyzes video content, not static images.
explanations.C: Correct. The Cloud Vision API is a pre-trained machine learning service that detects and categorizes objects, labels, and content within static images.
explanations.D: Incorrect. AutoML Tables builds models from tabular/structured data, not images.

question: Your organization runs all its workloads on Compute Engine virtual machine instances. Your organization has a security requirement: the virtual machines are not allowed to access the public internet. The workloads running on those virtual machines need to access BigQuery and Cloud Storage, using their publicly accessible interfaces, without violating the security requirement. Which Google Cloud product or feature should your organization use?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Identity-Aware Proxy controls inbound user access to applications; it does not let VMs without external IPs reach Google APIs.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Cloud NAT enables outbound access to the public internet, which would violate the requirement that VMs not access the internet.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Internal load balancers distribute traffic within a VPC; they do not provide access to Google APIs like BigQuery and Cloud Storage.
explanations.D: Correct. Private Google Access lets VMs that have no external IP address reach Google APIs and services (such as BigQuery and Cloud Storage) over Google's internal network, without using the public internet.

question: Which Google Cloud product is designed to reduce the risks of handling personally identifiable information (PII)?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Cloud Storage stores objects but does not by itself discover or de-identify sensitive PII.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Google Cloud Armor protects web applications from DDoS and web attacks; it does not handle PII discovery or redaction.
explanations.C: Correct. Cloud Data Loss Prevention (Cloud DLP / Sensitive Data Protection) discovers, classifies, and de-identifies (masks/redacts) sensitive data such as PII, directly reducing the risk of handling it.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Secret Manager securely stores credentials and API keys; it is not designed to find or de-identify PII within data.

question: Your organization is migrating to Google Cloud. As part of that effort, it needs to move terabytes of data from on-premises file servers to Cloud Storage. Your organization wants the migration process to be automated and to be managed by Google. Your organization has an existing Dedicated Interconnect connection that it wants to use. Which Google Cloud product or feature should your organization use?

explanations.A: Correct. Storage Transfer Service is a Google-managed, automated service that moves large volumes of data from on-premises file systems into Cloud Storage over the network, leveraging the existing Interconnect.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Migrate for Anthos modernizes VM workloads into containers; it does not perform file-data transfers to Cloud Storage.
explanations.C: Incorrect. BigQuery Data Transfer Service loads data into BigQuery from specific sources, not file-server data into Cloud Storage.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Transfer Appliance is a physical shipped device used when there is no good network connection; it is unnecessary when a Dedicated Interconnect is already available.

question: Your organization needs to analyze data in order to gather insights into its daily operations. You only want to pay for the data you store and the queries you perform. Which Google Cloud product should your organization choose for its data analytics warehouse?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Cloud SQL is a transactional relational database billed by running instances, not a pay-per-query analytics warehouse.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Dataproc runs managed Hadoop/Spark clusters that you pay for while running; it is not a serverless pay-per-query warehouse.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Cloud Spanner is a transactional relational database billed by provisioned capacity, not a query-based analytics warehouse.
explanations.D: Correct. BigQuery is a serverless data warehouse where you pay only for the storage you use and the data scanned by your queries, matching the stated cost model.

question: Your organization wants to run a container-based application on Google Cloud. This application is expected to increase in complexity. You have a security need for fine-grained control of traffic between the containers. You also have an operational need to exercise fine-grained control over the application's scaling policies. What Google Cloud product or feature should your organization use?

explanations.A: Correct. GKE provides fine-grained control over container networking (network policies between pods) and detailed scaling policies (horizontal/vertical pod and cluster autoscaling), suiting a growing, complex containerized app.
explanations.B: Incorrect. App Engine abstracts away the infrastructure and does not give fine-grained control over inter-container traffic or detailed scaling policies.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Cloud Run is a simpler serverless container platform that does not offer the fine-grained network and scaling controls of Kubernetes.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Plain Compute Engine VMs do not natively orchestrate containers or provide the fine-grained container traffic and scaling controls required.

question: Which Google Cloud product or feature makes specific recommendations based on security risks and compliance violations?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Google Cloud firewalls enforce network traffic rules; they do not analyze risks or make compliance recommendations.
explanations.B: Correct. Security Command Center scans your resources, surfaces security risks and compliance violations, and provides specific recommendations to remediate them.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Cloud Deployment Manager provisions infrastructure from templates; it does not assess security or compliance.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Google Cloud Armor mitigates web attacks and DDoS; it does not provide security-risk and compliance recommendations across resources.

question: Which Google Cloud product provides a consistent platform for multi-cloud application deployments and extends other Google Cloud services to your organization's environment?

explanations.A: Incorrect. GKE manages Kubernetes clusters within Google Cloud, but on its own it is not the multi-cloud, hybrid management platform described.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Virtual Private Cloud provides networking within Google Cloud; it is not a multi-cloud application deployment platform.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Compute Engine provides VMs in Google Cloud; it does not deliver a consistent multi-cloud or on-premises management platform.
explanations.D: Correct. Anthos is Google's hybrid and multi-cloud platform that provides a consistent way to run and manage applications across clouds and on-premises while extending Google Cloud services to those environments.

question: Your organization is developing an application that will manage payments and online bank accounts located around the world. The most critical requirement for your database is that each transaction is handled consistently. Your organization anticipates almost unlimited growth in the amount of data stored. Which Google Cloud product should your organization choose?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Cloud SQL is a regional relational database with limited vertical scaling and does not provide global, near-unlimited horizontal scale.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Cloud Storage is object storage and cannot enforce transactional consistency for financial transactions.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Firestore is a NoSQL document database; while it scales, it is not the strongly consistent global relational SQL database designed for high-volume financial transactions.
explanations.D: Correct. Cloud Spanner is a globally distributed relational database offering strong (external) consistency for transactions plus virtually unlimited horizontal scale, ideal for global financial systems.

question: Your organization wants an economical solution to store data such as files, graphical images, and videos and to access and share them securely. Which Google Cloud product or service should your organization use?

explanations.A: Correct. Cloud Storage is economical object storage ideal for unstructured data such as files, images, and videos, with secure access control and easy sharing.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Cloud SQL is a relational database for structured transactional data, not for storing large binary files and media.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Cloud Spanner is a relational database for structured data, not cost-effective object storage for files and videos.
explanations.D: Incorrect. BigQuery is an analytics warehouse for structured data, not for storing and sharing media files.

question: Your organization wants to predict the behavior of visitors to its public website. To do that, you have decided to build a machine learning model. Your team has database-related skills but only basic machine learning skills, and would like to use those database skills. Which Google Cloud product or feature should your organization choose?

explanations.A: Correct. BigQuery ML lets teams build and train machine learning models using standard SQL inside BigQuery, leveraging existing database/SQL skills without deep ML expertise.
explanations.B: Incorrect. LookML is the modeling language for the Looker BI tool; it is for defining business metrics, not building ML models.
explanations.C: Incorrect. TensorFlow is a powerful ML framework but requires substantial machine learning and programming expertise the team lacks.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Cloud SQL is a transactional relational database and does not provide built-in machine learning capabilities.

question: Your organization needs to restrict access to a Cloud Storage bucket. Only employees who are based in Canada should be allowed to view the contents. What is the most effective and efficient way to satisfy this requirement?

options.A: Deploy the Cloud Storage bucket to a Google Cloud region in Canada
options.B: Configure Google Cloud Armor to allow access to the bucket only from IP addresses based in Canada
options.C: Give each employee who is based in Canada access to the bucket
options.D: Create a group consisting of all Canada-based employees, and give the group access to the bucket

explanations.A: Incorrect. The region where a bucket is stored controls data residency, not which employees may view its contents.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Restricting by IP address is fragile (employees may travel or use VPNs) and Cloud Armor is not the mechanism for IAM-based bucket access control.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Granting access employee-by-employee is inefficient and hard to maintain as staff change.
explanations.D: Correct. Creating a Google group of Canada-based employees and granting the group access follows IAM best practice, making access efficient to manage and easy to update as membership changes.

question: Your organization is moving an application to Google Cloud. As part of that effort, it needs to migrate the application's working database from another cloud provider to Cloud SQL. The database runs on the MySQL engine. The migration must cause minimal disruption to users. Data must be secured while in transit. Which should your organization use?

explanations.A: Incorrect. BigQuery Data Transfer Service loads data into BigQuery for analytics, not for migrating a live MySQL database into Cloud SQL.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Manual MySQL batch inserts cause downtime and lack the continuous replication needed for minimal-disruption migration.
explanations.C: Correct. Database Migration Service performs minimal-downtime, continuous migrations of MySQL databases into Cloud SQL with encrypted (secure in-transit) connections.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Cloud Composer orchestrates workflows (Apache Airflow); it is not a purpose-built database migration tool.

question: Your organization is developing and deploying an application on Google Cloud. Tracking your Google Cloud spending needs to stay as simple as possible. What should you do to ensure that workloads in the development environment are fully isolated from production workloads?

options.A: Apply a unique tag to development resources
options.B: Associate the development resources with their own network
options.C: Associate the development resources with their own billing account
options.D: Put the development resources in their own project

explanations.A: Incorrect. Tags/labels help with cost tracking but do not provide true isolation of resources between environments.
explanations.B: Incorrect. A separate network isolates networking only, not IAM, quotas, or full resource boundaries between dev and production.
explanations.C: Incorrect. A separate billing account separates billing but is unnecessary for isolation and complicates spend tracking rather than keeping it simple.
explanations.D: Correct. Placing development resources in their own project provides full isolation (separate IAM, quotas, and resources) while keeping spend tracking simple because costs roll up per project.

question: Your company is running the majority of its workloads in a co-located data center. The workloads are running on virtual machines (VMs) on top of a hypervisor and use either Linux or Windows server editions. As part of your company's transformation strategy, you need to modernize workloads as much as possible by adopting cloud-native technologies. You need to migrate the workloads into Google Cloud. What should you do?

options.A: Export the VMs into VMDK format, and import them into Compute Engine
options.B: Export the VMs into VMDK format, and import them into Google Cloud VMware Engine
options.C: Migrate the workloads using Migrate for Compute Engine
options.D: Migrate the workloads using Migrate for Anthos

explanations.A: Incorrect. Importing VMs as-is into Compute Engine is a lift-and-shift that keeps the workloads as VMs and does not modernize them to cloud-native technologies.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Google Cloud VMware Engine keeps workloads as VMware VMs, which is the least modernized path, not cloud-native adoption.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Migrate for Compute Engine moves VMs into Compute Engine VMs (lift-and-shift); it does not modernize them into containers.
explanations.D: Correct. Migrate for Anthos converts VM-based workloads into containers running on GKE/Anthos, achieving the goal of adopting cloud-native technologies.

question: Your organization is running all its workloads in a private cloud on top of a hypervisor. Your organization has decided it wants to move to Google Cloud as quickly as possible. Your organization wants minimal changes to the current environment, while using the maximum amount of managed services Google offers. What should your organization do?

options.A: Migrate the workloads to Google Cloud VMware Engine
options.B: Migrate the workloads to Compute Engine
options.C: Migrate the workloads to Bare Metal Solution
options.D: Migrate the workloads to Google Kubernetes Engine

explanations.A: Incorrect. VMware Engine is best when you want to keep the existing VMware stack; it offers fewer of Google's broader managed services than Compute Engine and is aimed at VMware-specific environments.
explanations.B: Correct. Migrating the hypervisor-based VMs to Compute Engine is a fast lift-and-shift with minimal changes, while placing workloads on Google Cloud where they can leverage the maximum range of Google's managed services.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Bare Metal Solution is for specialized workloads needing dedicated hardware (e.g., certain Oracle databases); it provides the fewest managed services and is not the general fast-migration choice.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Moving to GKE requires re-architecting workloads into containers, which is a significant change, contradicting the requirement for minimal changes and speed.

question: Your organization is releasing its first publicly available application in Google Cloud. The application is critical to your business and customers and requires a 2- hour SLA. How should your organization set up support to minimize costs?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Premium Support offers the fastest response (around 15 minutes for critical cases) but at the highest cost, more than needed to meet a 2-hour target.
explanations.B: Correct. Enhanced Support provides a response time (about 1 hour for critical P1 cases) that meets the 2-hour requirement at a lower cost than Premium Support.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Standard Support's response times are too slow to reliably meet a 2-hour critical-case requirement for a business-critical application.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Basic Support does not include technical case support with response-time commitments, so it cannot meet a 2-hour SLA.

question: Your organization offers public mobile apps and websites. You want to migrate to a Google Cloud-based solution for checking and maintaining your users' usernames and passwords and controlling their access to different resources based on their identity. Which should your organization choose?

explanations.A: Incorrect. VPN tunnels provide encrypted network connectivity; they do not manage end-user identities, usernames, or passwords.
explanations.B: Correct. Identity Platform is a customer identity and access management (CIAM) service that authenticates app/website users (usernames, passwords, federated logins) and controls access based on their identity.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Firewall rules control network traffic to VMs; they do not authenticate application end users.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Private Google Access lets VMs reach Google APIs without external IPs; it is unrelated to managing end-user identities.

question: Which Google Cloud service or feature lets you build machine learning models using Standard SQL and data in a data warehouse?

explanations.A: Correct. BigQuery ML lets you create and run machine learning models directly in the BigQuery data warehouse using standard SQL.
explanations.B: Incorrect. TensorFlow is a programmatic ML framework that uses Python, not standard SQL within a data warehouse.
explanations.C: Incorrect. AutoML Tables builds models through a no-code interface on tabular data; it is not a SQL-based capability inside the data warehouse.
explanations.D: Incorrect. There is no Cloud Bigtable ML product; Bigtable is a NoSQL database without built-in SQL model training.

question: Your organization runs an application on virtual machines in Google Cloud. This application processes incoming images. This activity takes hours to create a result for each image. The workload for this application normally stays at a certain baseline level, but at regular intervals it spikes to a much greater workload. Your organization needs to control the cost to run this application. What should your organization do?

options.A: Purchase committed use discounts for the baseline load
options.B: Purchase committed use discounts for the expected spike load
options.C: Leverage sustained use discounts for your virtual machines
options.D: Run the workload on preemptible VM instances

explanations.A: Correct. The baseline load runs continuously, so committing to that capacity with committed use discounts (CUDs) yields significant savings, while spikes can be handled with on-demand capacity.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Committing to the spike capacity wastes money because that capacity is only needed occasionally and would sit paid-for but idle the rest of the time.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Sustained use discounts apply automatically and require no commitment, but they provide smaller savings than committing to the known steady baseline load.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Preemptible VMs can be interrupted at any time, which is risky for image processing that takes hours per result and could lose in-progress work.

question: Your organization is developing a plan for migrating to Google Cloud. What is a best practice when initially configuring your Google Cloud environment?

options.A: Create a project via Google Cloud Console per department in your company
options.B: Define your resource hierarchy with an organization node on top
options.C: Create projects based on team members' requests
options.D: Make every member of your company the project owner

explanations.A: Incorrect. Creating projects per department without first establishing the overarching hierarchy leads to disorganized, hard-to-govern resources.
explanations.B: Correct. The best practice is to define a resource hierarchy with an organization node at the top, which enables centralized policy, IAM, and billing inheritance across all folders and projects.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Creating projects ad hoc based on individual requests produces sprawl and weak governance instead of a planned structure.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Making everyone a project owner violates the principle of least privilege and creates serious security risks.
